review.review: The full recording confirms death: decision 1230, accepted log line 3737, explicitly identifies a gnoll scout as the killer. Earlier fly exchanges depleted health while magic was exhausted. A concrete preparation omission precedes that fallback: decision 867, accepted line 2478, publicly reveals a cursed disintegration wand. Decisions 878 and 888 (lines 2502 and 2532) retain that spare and an identified remove-curse scroll during quiet observations, but the equipped-only cleanse selector ignores the wand. Decision 1126 (line 3297) still carries both while the staff is empty and physical fly fallback begins. The focused correction permits conservative quiet spare-wand cleansing and preserves its menu target across bags, without claiming cleansing or charges before public confirmation. The new five-test regression has three expected assertion failures against original selectors and passes on the candidate; the full suite passes 2,005 tests with four skips. Fixtures are public-evidence reductions and independent UI contracts, not reconstructed original runtime memory or a changed-policy replay. This establishes a preparation defect, not that repairing it would prevent death. Historical backlog cases were not revalidated.
review.learnings: A wand need not be equipped to justify cleansing. Prepare a publicly known cursed spare during a quiet, freshly observed opportunity, preserve worn-curse priority, and keep its target through bag navigation. Do not infer successful cleansing, charge capacity or survival from choosing preparation.
